exit_plan: Enter at the next session's open, not at the signal close, and skip it if it opens past T1 or below the stop.
Sell one third at T1, one third at T2, the last third at T3.
After T1, move the stop on the rest to your entry. After T2, move it to T1.
If a session gaps through the stop, you are out at the open, not at the stop price.
If nothing has resolved by the time limit, exit what is left at that day's close.
Size so that a stop-out costs an amount you can afford to lose repeatedly. The stop is the plan; the targets are the hope.

rank.name: Rank
rank.tagline: Ranks every stock against the market and keeps the strongest
rank.style: Swing to positional, about a month
how: A gradient-boosted model reads 59 measures of each stock every evening: momentum, volatility, volume, trend, its position against its own sector benchmark, and the state of the market.
It was trained to rank stocks by how much they beat the market's median over the next 21 sessions, and nothing else.
The three highest-ranked stocks each session become signals.
rank.status_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, but the skill is not statistically clear among the 300 most-traded stocks.
rank.ranking_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, but the skill is not statistically clear among the 300 most-traded stocks.
rank.trading_why: Holdout trades averaged +0.17R after costs (month-clustered t +1.42): positive, but too noisy to rule out luck. Random picks with the same exits made -0.06R.
rank.alert_why: Alerts on: it ranks better than chance and its holdout trades made money after costs.

barrier.name: Barrier
barrier.tagline: The odds that a stock reaches its target before its stop
how: A classifier learns, from every stock-day in the past, whether a +3 ATR target was touched before a -1.5 ATR stop within 15 sessions.
Each evening it scores every stock with that probability; the base rate across the market is about one in four.
The three most probable become signals, with exactly those barriers as the stop and the second target.
barrier.status_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, but the holdout result is too short or noisy to rule out luck.
barrier.ranking_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, but the holdout result is too short or noisy to rule out luck.
barrier.trading_why: Holdout trades averaged -0.04R after costs (month-clustered t -1.00): indistinguishable from zero. It beat random picks by +0.05R, but that is not a profit.
barrier.alert_why: Alerts off: its holdout trades did not make money after costs. Its signals are shown on the site, never pushed.

relative.name: Relative
relative.tagline: Picks the stocks most likely to beat their own sector benchmark
how: Every stock is judged against its own benchmark: Nifty IT, Nifty Pharma and Nifty Bank where those exist, otherwise an index of its industry built from its peers.
The model is trained to rank stocks inside their own group by how far they beat that group's median over the next 21 sessions. The sector's own move is removed, so what is left is stock selection.
Because it carries the group's momentum, breadth and trend as inputs, it knows when a sector is strong or weak, and the three best-ranked stocks become signals.
relative.status_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, but the skill is not statistically clear among the 300 most-traded stocks.
relative.ranking_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, but the skill is not statistically clear among the 300 most-traded stocks.
relative.trading_why: Holdout trades averaged +0.18R after costs (month-clustered t +0.91): positive, but too noisy to rule out luck. Random picks with the same exits made -0.06R.
relative.alert_why: Alerts on: it ranks better than chance and its holdout trades made money after costs.

snapback.name: Snapback
snapback.tagline: The shortest horizon: who beats the market over the next week
how: The same inputs as Rank, but trained to rank stocks by their return over the next 5 sessions, so it learns short-term effects such as exhaustion and snap-back that a one-month model averages away.
The three highest-ranked become signals, with a tight stop and a one-week limit.
snapback.status_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, the holdout result is statistically solid, and the skill survives among the 300 most-traded stocks.
snapback.ranking_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, the holdout result is statistically solid, and the skill survives among the 300 most-traded stocks.
snapback.trading_why: Holdout trades averaged +0.02R after costs (month-clustered t -0.05): indistinguishable from zero. It beat random picks by +0.08R, but that is not a profit.
snapback.alert_why: Alerts off: its holdout trades did not make money after costs. Its signals are shown on the site, never pushed.

compounder.name: Compounder
compounder.tagline: The longest horizon: which stocks keep beating the market for six months
how: Trained to rank stocks by their return over the next 126 sessions (about six months) against the market's median.
It leans on persistence: multi-month momentum, steadiness of the trend, drawdown recovery and sector strength.
The three highest-ranked become signals, with a wide stop and a six-month limit.
compounder.status_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, but the holdout result is too short or noisy to rule out luck and the skill is not statistically clear among the 300 most-traded stocks.
compounder.ranking_why: Its scores ranked stocks better than chance in both periods, but the holdout result is too short or noisy to rule out luck and the skill is not statistically clear among the 300 most-traded stocks.
compounder.trading_why: Holdout trades averaged +0.25R after costs (month-clustered t +1.41): positive, but too noisy to rule out luck. Random picks with the same exits made -0.11R.
compounder.alert_why: Alerts on: it ranks better than chance and its holdout trades made money after costs.
